report.tagline: Anthropic's AI assistant for work: writing, coding and agents that do real tasks on your computer, with no ads.
report.simpleSummary: Claude is an AI you chat with, like ChatGPT, made by a company called Anthropic. People mostly use it for work: writing, coding, analysing documents and now handing over whole tasks. Tools like Claude Code and Cowork let it work directly on your files and computer, not just answer in a chat box. It has a free plan, but most of its money comes from businesses and paid plans, and it shows no ads.

keyNumbers.note: Bloomberg and FT figures summarised by Second Talent, up from about $9 billion at end of 2025. Most of this is API and business use, not the consumer app.

overview.whatItDoes: Claude answers questions, writes and edits, reads long documents, writes and runs code, and increasingly does multi-step work on its own. Claude Code works inside a developer's code project. Cowork lets non-developers give Claude a folder and a task, such as building a report from files. Claude Design turns a prompt into visual designs, slides and prototypes.
howItWorks: You chat on the web, desktop or phone app, and pick a model: Haiku (fast), Sonnet (balanced) or Opus (strongest).
Projects hold files and instructions so Claude remembers the context of ongoing work.
Artifacts show code, documents and small apps in a side panel you can edit and share.
Claude Code and Cowork let Claude read, write and run things on your computer, asking permission for risky steps.
Connectors link Claude to tools like Google Drive, Gmail, Slack and GitHub so it can pull in your work data.
Paid plans give more usage; limits reset every few hours and weekly.
overview.valueProposition: An AI colleague that can actually finish work tasks, especially coding and documents, with a reputation for careful answers and no ads.

frustrations: Max plan at $100 or $200 a month is a lot in rupees

personas.name: Knowledge worker
personas.description: A consultant or analyst who uses Claude and Cowork to turn piles of documents and spreadsheets into reports and slides.
goals: Cut report prep from days to hours
Trust the summary of long documents
frustrations: Not sure which plan has enough usage
Less consumer polish than ChatGPT, such as fewer voice and image features

personas.name: Enterprise buyer
personas.description: A CTO at a bank or software firm choosing which AI to give 5,000 employees and which model to build products on.
goals: Safe, reliable AI with strong data controls
One vendor for chat, coding and API
frustrations: Cost of heavy agent use is hard to predict
Microsoft and Google bundle AI into tools the company already pays for
Rapid model changes need constant re-testing

painPoints.pain: Developers spend hours on repetitive coding, debugging and tests.
painPoints.howSolved: Claude Code reads the whole project, makes changes across files and runs tests on its own.

painPoints.pain: Long contracts, research papers and reports take hours to read.
painPoints.howSolved: Claude can read very long documents in one go and answer questions about them.

painPoints.pain: Most AI chat tools give advice but leave you to do the work.
painPoints.howSolved: Cowork and agents take a task and produce the finished file, spreadsheet or deck.

painPoints.pain: Non-designers struggle to make decent slides, mockups and visuals.
painPoints.howSolved: Claude Design creates designs and prototypes from a plain description.

painPoints.pain: Companies worry about AI leaking data or saying harmful things.
painPoints.howSolved: Anthropic sells on safety, admin controls and not training on business data by default.

painPoints.pain: Ads in free AI apps make people wonder if answers are paid for.
painPoints.howSolved: Claude has no ads, and Anthropic made that a public promise in its 2026 marketing.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: An agent that works in your terminal, IDE or browser to write, edit and run code across a whole project.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Coding is the use case where Claude leads, and it drives a large share of paid plans and API spend.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: A desktop agent for non-coders: give it access to a folder and a task, and it produces finished files.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Takes the Claude Code idea to office workers, a much bigger market.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Creates visual designs, slides and clickable prototypes from a prompt.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Pulls in product, marketing and design users, and competes with tools like Canva and Figma for early drafts.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Projects store files and instructions; Artifacts show documents, code and mini apps you can edit and share.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Makes Claude a place where work lives, which brings users back.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Links Claude to Gmail, Google Drive, Slack, GitHub and many other tools.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Lets Claude use real work data, which makes answers more useful and harder to replace.

businessModel.summary: Claude makes money from paid plans and, much more, from businesses: Team and Enterprise seats plus pay-per-use API access for companies building on its models. There are no ads. Heavy agent use costs a lot of computing, so pricing and usage limits are a constant balancing act.

revenueStreams.detail: Developers and companies pay per token (small chunks of text). The largest share of Anthropic revenue, including through Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud.
Pro at $20 a month and Max at $100 or $200 a month. Paid subscribers more than doubled in 2026.
Per-user fees for businesses, plus usage charges for heavy agent work.
Sold inside Pro, Max and business plans; passed a $2.5 billion run rate by February 2026.

businessModel.pricing: Free; Pro $20 a month ($17 billed yearly); Max $100 or $200 a month for 5x or 20x Pro usage; Team $25 per seat a month; Enterprise custom. API per million tokens ranges from about $1 input for Haiku to $10 input and $50 output for the top model.
costDrivers: Computing to run models, especially long agent sessions that use many tokens
Training each new model generation on huge chip clusters, including a reported $100 billion-plus AWS deal
Safety research and testing before launches
businessModel.unitEconomics: A Pro user pays $20 a month. A light chat user might cost $2 to $5 in computing, so Anthropic keeps most of it. A heavy Claude Code user on Max at $200 can burn far more than $200 of computing in a month, which is why Anthropic added weekly limits. The money mostly works on the business side: API customers pay per token used, so revenue rises with cost. Rough estimates; Anthropic does not publish per-user figures.

howTheyGetUsers: Developer word of mouth: Claude Code spread through engineers sharing results
Enterprise sales and cloud marketplaces like AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex
Launches like Cowork and Claude Design that create new reasons to try it
Brand campaigns, including 2026 Super Bowl ads promising no ads in Claude
Integrations in tools people already use, such as Slack, Excel and developer IDEs
whatBringsUsersBack: Daily coding and work tasks that become a habit
Projects and memory that keep context
Usage limits that reset, nudging steady use and upgrades
Frequent model upgrades that improve results
growth.moat: Claude's edge is model quality for coding and long agent tasks, plus trust with businesses. Developers build workflows and company setups around Claude Code, which takes effort to switch. But rivals can catch up on model quality, so the moat depends on staying ahead and on business relationships.

competitors.name: ChatGPT
competitors.positioning: The largest consumer AI app, with about a billion weekly users, ads, voice and images.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Claude is much smaller with consumers but focuses on work, coding and agents, and has no ads.

competitors.name: Google Gemini
competitors.positioning: AI bundled with Android, Search and Workspace.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Claude has no phone or search distribution, so it wins by being better at specific jobs.

competitors.name: Cursor
competitors.positioning: AI code editor popular with developers.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Cursor is a partner and a rival: it uses Claude models but also competes with Claude Code for the same developers.

competitors.name: Microsoft Copilot
competitors.positioning: AI in Office and GitHub, sold through Microsoft 365 contracts.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Claude is a standalone choice; Copilot is bundled, which makes it the default in many companies.

northStar.metric: Weekly tasks completed by Claude that users accept (code changes merged, files delivered, answers kept)
northStar.why: Claude's value is finished work, not chat volume. Accepted tasks capture both quality and depth of use, and they drive paid upgrades and API spend.

strengths: Widely seen as the best AI for coding and long agent tasks in 2025 to 2026
Fast-growing business revenue, with a reported profit in Q2 2026
Trusted by enterprises; more US businesses pay for Anthropic than OpenAI by one Ramp measure
weaknesses: Far smaller consumer reach than ChatGPT and Gemini
Usage limits frustrate paying users, especially on Max
Fewer consumer extras like rich voice, image and video generation
Heavy reliance on cloud partners Amazon and Google for computing
risks: OpenAI, Google and open models from China catching up in coding
Partners like Cursor building their own models
AI regulation in the US, EU and elsewhere
Agent mistakes on real files or systems causing a public incident
userComplaints: Usage limits draining faster than expected, with a wave of complaints in March 2026 from Max subscribers
Surprise changes to limits without clear notice, reported by The Register in January 2026
Price too high for many users outside the US, such as students in India
Sometimes refuses or over-hedges on harmless requests
Occasional outages and slowdowns at peak times

improvementIdeas.idea: Live usage meter with a forecast: 'At this rate you will hit your limit Thursday'
improvementIdeas.problem: Paying users are surprised when limits run out mid-task.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer angry complaints and more planned upgrades.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Support tickets about limits and Pro to Max upgrade rate

improvementIdeas.idea: India pricing: a lower-priced Pro plan in rupees for students and solo developers
improvementIdeas.problem: India is Claude's second-largest web market but $20 to $200 is steep there.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More paying users in a fast-growing market before rivals lock them in.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Free to paid conversion in India

improvementIdeas.idea: Cowork starter templates for common office jobs, such as monthly reports, invoice checks and meeting packs
improvementIdeas.problem: Non-coders do not know what to ask an agent.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More Cowork tasks per user and stronger habits.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Agent sessions per user among non-developers

improvementIdeas.idea: Cheaper 'background mode' that runs long tasks overnight at lower cost
improvementIdeas.problem: Heavy agent tasks cost a lot and hit limits.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More work done per dollar of computing.

pmLessons: You do not need the most users to win. Claude picked work and coding, and grew revenue faster than bigger rivals.
Agents change the cost model: heavy users can cost more than they pay, so pricing and limits are product decisions.
Partners can also be competitors. Selling models to Cursor while building Claude Code needs careful choices.
Clear communication about limits matters as much as the limits themselves.

interviewQuestions.question: Claude has far fewer consumer users than ChatGPT. Should it chase consumers or double down on work?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare revenue per user and cost to serve in each segment. Note distribution gaps. Recommend a focus, and name one consumer bet that supports work use.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you design usage limits for the Max plan?
interviewQuestions.hint: Balance user trust, computing cost and fairness. Options: weekly caps, priority tiers, pay-as-you-go top-ups. Show the meter clearly. Track churn and cost per user.

interviewQuestions.question: What should be the north star metric for Cowork?
interviewQuestions.hint: Pick a metric that shows finished work, like accepted tasks per week. Break it into adoption, task volume and quality. Add guardrails for mistakes on user files.

interviewQuestions.question: Cursor uses Claude models but competes with Claude Code. How would you manage this?
interviewQuestions.hint: Map what each side gains. API revenue vs. owning the user. Discuss when to compete, when to partner, and how to differentiate Claude Code.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow Claude in India?
interviewQuestions.hint: Use data: India is about 11 percent of web visits. Look at pricing in rupees, student plans, local payment methods like UPI, and Indic language quality. Pick one and set a metric.
